item.name: Camera 1
item.warningSigns: The threat is seen through the camera feed instead of normal room treatment.
item.bestAction: Stay focused on the camera clue and stop treating the moment like a normal patient task.
item.consequence: Ignoring the camera event lets the threat keep advancing through the run.
item.cardSummary: Camera 1 is the first surveillance-style anomaly. It matters because the clue comes from the camera view, not from a patient standing in front of you.

item.name: Camera 2
item.warningSigns: A second abnormal camera moment appears after the first camera event.
item.bestAction: Check the camera feed carefully and react before returning to normal treatment.
item.consequence: Missing the second camera clue can turn the camera sequence into a run-ending threat.
item.cardSummary: Camera 2 is the follow-up surveillance anomaly. Treat it as a separate warning because it appears after the first camera scare.

item.name: Bed Monster
item.warningSigns: The patient bed becomes the center of the threat instead of a normal treatment spot.
item.bestAction: Back away from the bed threat and avoid standing close while the anomaly is active.
item.consequence: Treating the bed like a normal patient station can put the player inside the danger zone.
item.cardSummary: Bed Monster turns a normal treatment bed into the threat. The useful clue is the bed itself changing from safe station to hazard.

item.name: Fire
item.warningSigns: A room hazard starts burning instead of behaving like a normal patient event.
item.bestAction: Move away from the flames and avoid staying in the burning area.
item.consequence: Standing in the fire hazard can punish the player before the shift continues.
item.cardSummary: Fire is a direct room hazard. It is easier to read than a hidden monster because the danger is the burning area itself.

item.name: Slime
item.warningSigns: Slime appears as the abnormal object or surface in the room.
item.bestAction: Keep clear of the slime and avoid walking into the hazard while handling the room.
item.consequence: Touching or ignoring the slime can turn a simple room check into a danger moment.
item.cardSummary: Slime is a floor or room hazard style anomaly. Watch the room surface before rushing back into treatment.

item.name: Eyes
item.warningSigns: Eyes appear where the room or patient should look normal.
item.bestAction: Stop rushing the treatment and respond to the visual clue before moving on.
item.consequence: Overlooking the eyes can leave the player reacting late to the anomaly.
item.cardSummary: Eyes is a visual warning anomaly. It is the kind of threat players can miss if they only focus on the next treatment prompt.

item.name: Tentacles Monster
item.warningSigns: Tentacles appear as the main abnormal shape in the room.
item.bestAction: Keep distance from the tentacles and avoid treating the room like a safe station.
item.consequence: Standing too close to the monster hazard can turn the encounter into a fail state.
item.cardSummary: Tentacles Monster is a body-horror room threat. The tentacles are the warning that the room has stopped being safe.

item.name: Death Ritual: Remove Candles
item.warningSigns: A ritual setup appears with candles that can be removed.
item.bestAction: Remove all candles when you want the intervention path.
item.consequence: Removing the candles changes the ritual outcome instead of letting the patient die.
item.cardSummary: This Death Ritual variant is the active intervention path. The key action is removing every candle before accepting the outcome.

item.name: Death Ritual: Let Patient Die
item.warningSigns: The same candle ritual appears, but the player allows the death outcome.
item.bestAction: Let the ritual finish only when you want to see the death-path outcome.
item.consequence: The patient dies and the ritual path resolves differently from the candle-removal route.
item.cardSummary: This Death Ritual variant is the non-intervention path. It is useful to track separately because the choice changes the outcome.

item.name: Eyeless: Talk
item.warningSigns: An eyeless character appears and can be approached as a dialogue choice.
item.bestAction: Talk to Eyeless when you want the dialogue-path outcome.
item.consequence: Talking triggers one branch of the Eyeless encounter.
item.cardSummary: This Eyeless variant tracks the talk choice. It belongs apart from the ignore route because the player action is different.

item.name: Eyeless: Ignore
item.warningSigns: Eyeless appears, but the player can choose not to talk.
item.bestAction: Ignore Eyeless when you want the alternate no-dialogue outcome.
item.consequence: Ignoring him triggers the alternate Eyeless branch.
item.cardSummary: This Eyeless variant tracks the ignore choice. It is separate because the same encounter can play out differently.

item.name: Black Bunny
item.warningSigns: A dark bunny-like threat appears instead of a normal patient.
item.bestAction: Keep distance and treat the encounter as a chase or threat moment.
item.consequence: Letting the bunny close the gap can force a failure or escape panic.
item.cardSummary: Black Bunny is a hostile creature-style anomaly. It is less about diagnosis and more about recognizing the threat quickly.

item.name: Infector
item.warningSigns: The encounter centers on an infection-style threat instead of normal treatment.
item.bestAction: Avoid direct contact and handle the encounter as a spread or infection hazard.
item.consequence: Getting too close can let the infection threat punish the player or route.
item.cardSummary: Infector is the anomaly to treat as a contact danger. The name points to a threat that spreads or punishes close interaction.

item.name: T-Pose
item.warningSigns: A character or patient appears frozen in an unnatural T-pose.
item.bestAction: Do not ignore the pose change; keep space until the encounter resolves.
item.consequence: Treating the T-pose as harmless can leave the player open to the final threat.
item.cardSummary: T-Pose looks simple at first, but the abnormal pose is the warning. It belongs with the late hostile encounters because players may dismiss it too quickly.
